This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. merge_ruling.for_merge: THE TRAILING POINT IS THE ARGUMENT. The poll of 10 August 1833 reads 'Rider, Elia.' — with a full stop after the a, which is what an abbreviated middle initial carries and what a given name does not. 'Eli A.' mis-joined is exactly 'Elia.'. The other card is documented: 'Rider, Eli A.' on the 1834 poll, Fergus 1843 ('Rider, Eli A., clerk, Charles L. P. Hogan [went to Aurora, Ill.]'), Norris 1844 ('Rider, E. A. clerk at C. L. P. Hojran') and the Democrat of 10 September 1834 as 'Rider, E. A.'. The town holds exactly two Riders and they are these.
merge_ruling.against_merge: AND NO ONE ROLL SETS BOTH. 'Rider, Elia.' is the 1833 poll (voter_lists_1833_1835.txt line 44) and 'Rider, Eli A.' the 1834 poll (line 262): two of the four rolls the one transcription bundles, and neither carries the other reading. The Democrat likewise sets 'E. Rider' in one issue (1 October 1834, #c005) and 'Rider, E. A.' in another (10 September 1834, #c006) — two issues, never one. So the fold rests on a compositor's point being read as an abbreviation, which is an inference about a mark and not a printing caught varying. D9, and `for_merge` is kept because the 1833 poll's image would settle it at once.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE CONSOLIDATED CIVIC, CHURCH, PRESS, BOOK AND CENSUS EVIDENCE (T-0513, T-0514). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here is written unattested in its own block, because the lists that name this person name a person and not a family. What is claimed is that the sources cited on the member below name them at Chicago, and the grade is the owner's ratified ladder applied by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py --build and spent by tools/mint_civic_residents.py, which prints every refusal. docs/LIBERTIES.md L215 carries the liberty and the tension with L213.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. WHAT THIS PASS RULED ONTO THIS HOUSEHOLD, named so the ruling can be found again: each volume below is followed by the printed entries it set against this person and the status the crosswalk ruled them at — a single entry carries what its own `could_carry` declares, and an ambiguous or contested match carries nothing and is shown so that the silence is legible. rider_eli_a, Fergus's Chicago directory of 1839 — f1839_e1228 (a single entry); rider_eli_a, Fergus's Chicago directory of 1843 — f1843_e2096 (a single entry); rider_eli_a, Norris's Chicago directory of 1844 — n1844_e1487 (a single entry).

occupation_later.note: Fergus's Chicago directory of 1839 prints this trade against this person, in the entry quoted on the card: 'Rider, E. A., clerk, C. L. P. Hogan'. It is evidence about 1839, written here as 1839's and read back onto no 1835 claim. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. The value is the volume's own line, split by its crosswalk on the entry's punctuation. These volumes set the trade first and its qualifiers after it on the same line, so the split may carry an employer, a market or a corner along with the trade. The printed entry is quoted beside the value for exactly that reason: the split is checkable against it, and neither is read into an 1835 claim.
